title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Quantum tunnelling of the magnetization in Ln3+ SMMs is reduced by enforcing high local symmetry, particularly square-antiprismatic D4d, pentagonal-bipyramidal D5h, or linear D∞h coordination.
explanation: Ground-doublet QTM depends on dipolar interactions, hyperfine coupling, exchange, and deviation from high symmetry. Crystal-field control of the coordination environment is presented as the chemical route to suppress transverse anisotropy. Non-Kramers ions such as Tb3+ can still show degenerate ±mJ levels only when symmetry is tightly controlled, as in bis-phthalocyanine complexes.
scope: Ln3+ SMMs, including non-Kramers Tb3+ systems.
conditions: Accurate control of the lanthanide coordination geometry.
caveats: High symmetry is necessary but not sufficient; Raman and direct processes, and interactions in polynuclear compounds, can still limit blocking.
